newsitem.title: CANADA: MAPCO joins Canada's Alliance pipeline.
newsitem.headline: MAPCO joins Canada's Alliance pipeline.

text.p: Alliance Pipeline, a proposed C$3.6 billion project that would move natural gas to Chicago from northern Canada, said on Wednesday that U.S. natural gas liquids company MAPCO Inc bought a five percent stake in the partnership.

MAPCO joins 18 energy companies in the producer-backed pipeline that would compete with traditional pipeline companies like NOVA Corp and TransCanada PipeLines Ltd for the right to ship liquids-rich Canadian gas to U.S. Midwest markets.
Other Alliance partners include Alberta Energy Co Ltd, Gulf Canada Resources Ltd and IPL Energy Inc.

"MAPCO is a significant player in the North American energy industry and will strengthen the Alliance partnership," Alliance chief executive Dennis Cornelson said in a statement. "Their knowledge and understanding of the natural gas business in all its configurations will help Alliance pursue many diverse opportunities."
Tulsa, Oklahoma-based MAPCO has an extensive infrastructure of gathering, processing and distributing systems, which includes a full range of NGL marketing services.
The Alliance Pipeline project, which ship 1.3 billion cubic feet per day of gas to Chicago from northeastern British Columbia by 1999.
